log.why: E8 tests {fliC, gyrA} with combined prior 0.450, nearly bisectioning the probability mass for maximum information gain.
Treat at 3 µM to bisect the Ticket 2 prior probability mass (61% <= 3 µM vs 39% > 3 µM).
Test the leading candidate metJ directly; a positive result will give high confidence to publish.
E2 splits the remaining posterior mass nearly in half and will strongly confirm 3 uM if there is no response.
Test 10 µM on Ticket 3 to split its prior probability mass nearly in half while we prepare to publish Ticket 1.
Posterior for metJ is 0.932 after two informative plates, making immediate publication optimal for time and plate bonuses.
Test 30 µM on Ticket 3 to split the remaining high-dose probability mass while incubators are free before publishing Ticket 2.
Test {fliC, trpE, hisG} on Ticket 4 to bisect its prior (0.473 vs 0.527) before publishing Ticket 2 while plates incubate.
Ticket 2 has only 18 seconds left and a strong 0.730 posterior for 3 µM after positive E3 and negative E2.
Test at 100 µM to distinguish between the two remaining likely thresholds (100 µM and 300 µM) before Ticket 3 expires.
Test the leading candidate hisG directly to resolve the three remaining plausible genes.
Ticket 3 has only 11s left and a strong 0.846 posterior for 300 µM after negative responses up to 100 µM.
Both E11 and E4 gave positive results, strongly pointing to hisG with an 87.8% posterior probability before time runs out.
Testing at 1 uM splits the prior probability mass for Ticket 5 nearly in half (0.557 vs 0.443), maximizing information gain.
While Ticket 5 incubates, E3 on Ticket 6 bisects its prior near the median (0.586 cumulative probability at <= 3 uM).
Test 10 uM on Ticket 6 to strongly confirm 10 uM or shift to 30 uM before the round ends.
With only 12 seconds left in the round, publishing Ticket 5 has positive expected value and leaves time to publish Ticket 6 after E4.
